etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Contraction of その様(よう)な (sono yō na).
The interjective sense is an ellipsis of a phrase like そんなことはありえない！ (Sonna koto wa arienai!, “Such a thing is not possible!”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese. First attested in the Man'yōshū, compiled 759 CE.
There are various theories regarding the ultimate derivation:
* Being the initial ma- is from 目 (ma, me, “eye”), it was thought to be an alteration of 目前 (mesaki, “before one's eyes”), with the me- element becoming ma-, but there was no attestation of masaki.
* Compound of root 正 (masa, “exactly”, found in compounds such as まさに (masa ni, “certainly, exactly, without doubt”)) + か (ka, “special suffix indicating condition”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Believed to derive from 忙しい (sewashii, “busy”). The kanji are ateji (当(あ)て字(じ)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 作 (tsak, “to do, to work”). Compare Cantonese 作 (zok³), Wu 作.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 作(つく)る (tsukuru, “to make; to build; to work the land, to grow something”), itself from Old Japanese.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 作(つくり) (tsukuri) above. The -tsukuri changes to -zukuri as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. Possibly related to 少ない (sukunai). Possibly cognate with the ku part in 幾 (iku).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From earlier 炒(いた)む (itamu).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Literary Chinese 生產 (shēngchǎn, “procreation; reproduction; making a living; livelihood”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 祝(いわ)う (iwau, “to celebrate”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 繋(つな)がる (tsunagaru, “to be connected”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 臥(ふ)す (fusu) + 間(ま) (ma).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Irregular shift of the on'yomi pronunciation from au to ao, versus the expected development of /au/ → /ɔː/ → /oː/.
/au/ → /awo/ → /ao/
Compare 倒す (tafusu > ta(w)usu > tawosu > taosu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
*/uwu/ → /uweru/ → /ueru/
From classical verb 飢う (uu).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.
